summary.machine: RSW-LAB (laboratory pedestal spot welder) — not RSW-01

hypotheses.statement: Acceptable weld: the setpoints, force and current all lie inside the same-setpoint population, and the mean current sits only at its p90 edge.

Expulsion or splash: the current is erratic (2746 A to 4368 A), which is consistent with molten metal ejected at the faying interface or electrode contact. This would show as spatter, a burn mark or a crater on the surface.

Burn-through or surface overheating, or an undersized or missing nugget (cold weld or no fusion). Heat input may have been too high or the current unstable, leaving a hole, excessive indentation or a weak joint.
Electrode misalignment from the 15 degree electrode angle, causing an off-centre or irregular nugget.

requests.target: Electrode-side (top) face of the welded coupon at the weld spot
requests.how_to_shoot: Close-up perpendicular to the surface, in even lighting, with the weld spot centred and filling about half the frame. Include a scale (ruler or coin) if possible.
requests.why_this_photo: The logged values are in the normal range, so only the weld surface can separate a good weld from expulsion, burn-through or misalignment.

requests.target: Back (opposite) face of the welded coupon behind the weld spot
requests.how_to_shoot: Close-up perpendicular to the surface, in even lighting, with the spot centred. Also take one oblique shot to show any bulge or cracking.
requests.why_this_photo: The back face shows whether heat reached through the stack. A missing mark points to a cold weld, and a hole or spatter points to expulsion or burn-through.

Acceptable weld with no visible defect.

events.root_cause: I keep the expulsion conclusion and override my E2 declaration. E2 matched the "no hole, no bulge" observation I had said would support an acceptable weld. That observation only rules out burn-through, which is why H3 drops. It does not show the weld is acceptable. E1 matched the observation I declared as refuting H1 and supporting H2: a dark burn ring and a jagged metallic protrusion inside the indentation, with no clean smooth centre. Two declared outcomes conflict, and E1 is the more specific one. The photo reader also described the back as a dark heat-tint ring around a rough-textured nugget, not a faint mark, so E2 does not clearly show a clean weld either. The most likely mechanism is expulsion at the electrode contact, with erratic current (2746 A to 4368 A) and mean current at the p90 edge. The sheets joined with no burn-through, but the weld is flawed and should be rejected or sectioned to check nugget size.

conflicts: [E2] "Faint, round indentation or discolouration with no hole and no bulge" is visible. You declared it SUPPORTS H1 ("Acceptable weld: the setpoints, force and current all lie inside the same-setpoint population, and the mean current sits only at its p90 edge."), but your final ranking puts H2 first.
challenge.draft_root_cause: The weld has an expulsion-type defect. Heat or current was too high at the electrode-sheet contact, so molten metal was ejected and then froze as a jagged metallic protrusion inside the indentation, with a dark burn ring around it. The erratic logged current (2746 A to 4368 A) fits this. Force and peak current were normal, so it was not an equipment fault. The back face shows a fused nugget with a heat-tint ring and no hole or spatter, so the sheets joined and there was no burn-through. The weld is flawed, probably with a reduced or irregular nugget, and should be rejected or sectioned to check nugget size.
